steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
With two sentences, you'll make several files, move them into a folder and rename them all at once.

Today you'll learn three new things.

  1. Have it make several files at once
  2. Have it make a folder, move and rename files
  3. How to read a new permission screen: "May I run this command?" (Bash command)
  • Time: 15 minutes
  • You need: a computer that finished Terminal practice 3
Today you'll move files, so be sure to work only inside the Practice folder.

faq.q: Will I have it delete things?
faq.a: No. Today is only making, moving and renaming. You'll learn to deny delete commands if you see one.

steps.title: Which computer are you using?
steps.html: Pick the computer you used for Terminal practice 1.

steps.title: Start Claude Code in the practice folder
steps.html:
1. Double-click the Practice folder on your desktop.
  2. Click the address bar at the top of the folder window, type powershell → Enter.
  3. Type claude in the window → Enter. It's a new job, so start without -c.

check.q: Do you see the box to type in (with a > sign)?

win.html:
1. Double-click the Practice folder on your desktop.
  2. Click the address bar at the top of the folder window, type powershell → Enter.
  3. Type claude in the window → Enter. It's a new job, so start without -c.

mac.html:
1. Open Terminal. (⌘ command+space → Terminal → return)
  2. Type cd and a space, drag the Practice folder onto the window, and press return.
  3. Type claude → return. It's a new job, so start without -c.

steps.title: If it doesn't start
steps.html:
• If you see 'claude' is not recognized, close and reopen the window, or restart the computer.
  • Not sure? See 'Open the window in the practice folder' in Terminal practice 1 again.

steps.title: Make 3 memo files at once
steps.html: Type the sentence below and press {{enterkey}}. As in Terminal practice 1, a Create file permission screen appears once per file, three times. Check each file name and press {{enterkey}} on 1. Yes each time.
steps.alt: Three memo files appear in the Practice folder
steps.code: Create 3 memo files, meeting.txt, groceries.txt and ideas.txt, with a line or two of example text in each

check.q: Did you choose Yes all three times, and are there 3 new files in Practice?

steps.title: If some files are missing
steps.html:
• If you chose 3. No on any, that file wasn't made: "Also make the files you haven't made yet."
  • If the folder window was already open, close it and open it again.

steps.title: First, what's a 'command'?
steps.html:
So far Claude has created and edited the contents of files, with Create file / Edit file screens.

Making folders and moving files works by Claude giving your computer a short instruction in English (a command), the same kind of thing you pasted to install in Terminal practice 1. So this time a different permission screen appears: Bash command.

mkdirmake a folder
mvmove or rename

steps.title: Make a folder and move the files
steps.html: Send the sentence below and a new Bash command permission screen appears. Don't choose yet; just compare it with the picture.
steps.alt: Reading the command to run on the Bash command permission screen
steps.code: Make a memos folder and move the three files you just made into it

check.q: Did a Bash command screen appear, like the picture?

steps.title: If no Bash command screen appeared
steps.html:
• Claude may still be thinking. Wait a few seconds.
  • If it went ahead without asking, you may have chosen 2. Yes, and don't ask again before; then it won't ask for that kind of command again.

choices.label: Show how to read the screen

steps.title: How to read the 'May I run this command?' screen
steps.html:
Bash commandA screen asking "May I give your computer a command?"
The English line in the middleThe actual command to run
Grey text below itClaude's description. Read this part
1. YesYes, run it
2. Yes, and don't ask again…Run commands like this without asking → don't choose this for now
3. NoNo, do it differently

You don't need to understand the command. If the grey description matches your request, press {{enterkey}} on 1. Yes. With several commands it may ask several times.

Stop if you see these. rm, del and Remove-Item are commands that delete. If you didn't ask to delete, choose 3. No.

On Windows you may see New-Item or Move-Item.

check.q: Did the description match, and did you choose 1. Yes?

steps.title: If the description differs or is confusing
steps.html:
• That's exactly when to choose 3. No. Nothing changes.
  • Then ask again, e.g. "Just make a memos folder and move the three files into it. Don't delete anything."

steps.title: Rename all the files at once
steps.html: Add today's date to the front of the three file names. When the Bash command screen appears again, read the grey description and choose 1. Yes if it matches. The real date today is used.
steps.code: Add today's date to the front of the file names in the memos folder, e.g. 2026-11-24_meeting.txt

check.q: Did you read the description and choose 1. Yes?

steps.title: Check the result yourself
steps.html:
1. Open the Practice folder on your desktop. There's a new memos folder.
  2. Double-click it to open it.

If the 3 files are inside with the date in front of their names, it worked. When you're done, type /exit in the terminal or close the window.
steps.alt: Three files with dates in their names inside the memos folder

check.q: Are there 3 files with dates in their names in the memos folder?

steps.title: If the result looks different
steps.html:
• If the folder window was already open, close it and open it again.
  • If something moved to the wrong place or got an odd name: "Undo what you just did." Read the screen and choose Yes then too.

steps.title: 🎉 Terminal practice 4 done! What you learned
steps.html:
Something that would have meant moving and renaming files one by one took two sentences.

Create fileAsks when making file contents
Bash commandAsks when running a command, like making folders, moving or renaming
Grey descriptionRead just this, even if you don't know the command

Two things to remember

  1. Don't choose 2. Yes, and don't ask again until you're comfortable.
  2. If you see a delete command (rm, del, Remove-Item) you didn't ask for, choose 3. No.

Next step

You have the basics now. The Real work course (spreadsheets, summaries, report drafts…) uses desktop-app screens, but typing the same sentences in the terminal works the same way.
